# QS-CFW-5349-60 - Quality specification - track link CFW-5349-60 (15B37)
Revision: Rev C  
Supersedes: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-5349-60

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treatment, machining, and final inspection of track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60). It defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore geometry and maximum forging weight for all deliveries from Plant P1 for the listed part.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (through-hardened area) | 33-36 HRC | Measure on cross-section representative of wear surface |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.03 mm | Applies to finished bore after final machining |
| Maximum forging weight | 58.0 kg | Maximum blank weight prior to machining operations |

Inspection method
- Hardness: Verify hardness on the designated testing location using a calibrated Rockwell C hardness tester. Employ multiple indentations across the wear surface area to ensure uniformity representative of the part.
- Bore diameter: Inspect finished bores using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement systems capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Confirm measurement strategy produces traceable results to the organization calibration system.
- Forging weight: Record forging blank weight on calibrated scales at receipt from forging cell. Compare recorded value to the maximum forging weight requirement listed above.

Nonconformance handling
- Any unit failing to meet hardness, bore tolerance, or forging weight requirements shall be segregated and tagged. Cause shall be investigated and corrective actions documented in the local NCR system.
- If hardness is out of specification, material disposition must include root-cause analysis of heat treatment parameters and verification of corrective heat treatment trials before release.
- If bore diameter is out of tolerance, assess if rework is feasible within drawing limits; otherwise, part shall be rejected and returned to manufacturing for corrective action.
- If forging weight exceeds the maximum forging weight, reject and quarantine the lot; review forging process controls to prevent recurrence.

Related documents
- none
